proposed.explanation:
The verified evidence supports continuing to hold ABUK as your fertilizer-exporter currency hedge. The 9-month 2026 basic EPS of 8.74 EGP (verified) compares with 4.28 EGP for the same period a year earlier (verified), indicating earnings per share more than doubled year-over-year. Annualising the 9-month EPS roughly gives ~11.6 EGP, which against the current price of 76.21 EGP implies a P/E in the mid-6s – a reasonable valuation for a commodity-linked exporter with demonstrated earnings momentum. This aligns well with your stated goal of keeping a fertilizer exporter as a currency hedge over a 5-year horizon, and your medium risk tolerance is consistent with holding a single commodity-linked name that you already own.

I cannot recommend buying additional ABUK shares because your current 400 shares (worth 30,484 EGP) already represent about 60% of your total portfolio value (50,484 EGP), and the diversification rule caps any single holding at 50% after a buy. Buying more would deepen the concentration further. You also have no stated need to sell: the earnings trend is positive, the position matches your stated purpose, and your 5-year horizon gives the currency-hedge thesis time to play out.

Risks and uncertainties: (1) Several key figures – total net profit for both periods, the Q3-2026 EPS, and all percentage-change columns – are marked AMBIGUOUS due to OCR/unit issues, so I could not independently verify the absolute profit level or the exact Q3-2026 quarterly EPS. This limits the depth of the fundamental check. (2) Fertiliser prices are commodity-driven and can swing sharply; a 5-year horizon helps but does not eliminate drawdown risk. (3) The EGP-denominated currency-hedge benefit depends on the EGP/USD path, which is outside the evidence provided. (4) The low P/E could reflect market scepticism about sustainability of the earnings spike; a single 9-month result is not a multi-year trend. I recommend monitoring the next full-year report to confirm the earnings trajectory before considering any position change.
